# situation: a step uses actions/checkout by a commit SHA that only a fork
#   of actions/checkout has.
# reason: GitHub serves the commits of a repository's forks under the
#   repository's name, so the SHA, which reads as a pin of actions/checkout,
#   runs code that whoever pushed it to the fork wrote (the Trivy incident,
#   GHSA-69fq-xp46-6x23: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-69fq-xp46-6x23).
# attack: the rule reports the form in which someone pushes a commit to
#   their fork of actions/checkout and gets its SHA written in this workflow,
#   such as by a pull request from a fork that changes the SHA of the uses and
#   is merged. Background: in the Trivy incident of 2026-03-19, a commit
#   pushed with stolen credentials swapped the workflow's actions/checkout for
#   the impostor commit 70379aad; the credential premise leaves the holder of
#   such stolen credentials out of the threat model, but the workflow that the
#   incident left has the same form.
# attack-run-behavior: the runner fetches 70379aad by the name
#   actions/checkout, from the objects the fork network shares, and runs its
#   action as the step, in the job's workspace and environment; in the Trivy
#   incident it was a composite action that downloaded malicious Go source
#   files from a typosquatted domain, and the commit was tagged v0.69.4 so
#   that the release pipeline ran it.
# advisory: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-69fq-xp46-6x23
on: workflow_call
jobs:
  a:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@70379aad1a8b40919ce8b382d3cd7d0315cde1d0
